result: In a community cohort of 24,095 (548 with long COVID), people with symptoms beyond 12 weeks had significant sustained-attention deficits vs uninfected participants; path models showed direct COVID effects on attention and memory plus on-task fatigue build-up.
reason: Same domain (objective attention/memory deficits) in a long COVID population; adds the sustained-attention and fatigue-mediation detail

result: In 14 long COVID patients with Fitbit monitoring for a median 28 days, nocturnal RMSSD had no within-person day-to-day link with fatigue (r=-0.064), but people with higher average HRV reported less fatigue (beta=-1.26).
reason: No control group, so it cannot test the resting HRV case-control claim; it is a within-patient nocturnal HRV-symptom association

result: In 14 long COVID patients, wearable-measured sleep duration and REM sleep were associated within-person with next-day fatigue (r about -0.28 and -0.22); a sleep efficiency-energy association was judged likely chance.
reason: No controls and consumer-wearable sleep metrics; it does not test the PSG case-control sleep claim

result: ASL in 22 post-COVID patients vs 19 matched controls showed lower global CBF (49.2 vs 51.7 mL/100g/min) and regional hypoperfusion (e.g. right inferior occipital 27.9 vs 46.4), with slower reaction times on a 20-min PVT.
reason: Same measure (resting ASL CBF) and direction, but in long COVID rather than ME/CFS, so it extends rather than replicates; OI status not reported

result: In a representative survey of 9,620 NYC adults with prior COVID-19, 20.9% had PEM symptoms on the DSQ-PEM and 4.0% had PEM lasting 14 hours or more, with 3-4 times more mental health outcomes and 4-5 times higher disability scores.
reason: Measures PEM prevalence by cross-sectional survey, not new ME/CFS incidence by criteria vs uninfected participants

result: In a crossover RCT, 6 weeks of supervised exercise in PESE-negative long COVID adults produced no cytokine or immune-cell changes that survived FDR correction.
reason: Measures immune markers after training in PESE-negative patients, not post-exertional symptom worsening; no atlas finding covers training-related immune change

result: In 71 long COVID patients with fatigue, reduced P50 suppression on a paired-click EEG test was associated with higher MFIS cognitive fatigue (tau=-0.173, p=0.037), independent of depressive symptoms.
reason: neuro-sensory already covers P50 sensory gating; this adds a long COVID fatigue correlation (no control group)

result: In 58 post-COVID patients vs 22 controls, a 1-min maximal pinch produced a smaller post-exercise drop in MEP amplitude and no silent-period prolongation (or shortening), and both correlated with higher fatigue and exertion.
reason: Same mechanism (altered central motor regulation during and after sustained effort), measured by TMS in long COVID

result: EPIC v2 PBMC methylation in 188 women (71 ME/CFS, 44 FM, 73 controls) found, after cell-composition adjustment, a principal-component axis (PC5) separating ME/CFS and tied to PEM and cognitive symptoms, with 591 associated DMRs.
reason: Same measure (genome-wide blood methylation) with composition adjustment; it is a new single-cohort signal that still needs replication

result: MRI/DTI in 88 long COVID patients (33 bedridden) vs 34 controls found lower dorsal raphe, midbrain reticular formation and superior cerebellar peduncle volumes, lower middle cerebellar peduncle FA, and three mammillary-body volume phenotypes.
reason: Brainstem volume differences in a long COVID population; exploratory preprint without multiple-comparison correction
